heuristics.prefix: The value starts with a known credential prefix: sk-, sk-ant-, ghp_, gho_, github_pat_, xoxb-, AKIA, 'Bearer '. Prefix evidence is SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN — never AND it with an entropy gate (see POS-github-token-legacy and POS-aws-access-key-id).
heuristics.entropy: Shannon entropy over the value's own character distribution, in bits per character. Applicable ONLY to unprefixed, unstructured strings of length >= 32. See ./negative-cases.json → entropyFinding before choosing a threshold.
heuristics.shape: The value matches a credential-bearing structure: a JWT triplet, a PEM block, or any URL carrying a userinfo component (user:password before the @).

expectedFindings.why: 🔴 PREFIX-ONLY DISCRIMINATOR. Entropy 2.06 — below every value in this repository, synthetic or real. A detector that requires prefix AND entropy misses it. A real token with a long repeated run would be missed the same way.

🔴 SECOND PREFIX-ONLY DISCRIMINATOR, and the sharpest one: at 3.62 bits/char it is LOWER-entropy than every negative in ./negative-cases.json (3.73–4.21). Any entropy threshold that catches it also flags every git SHA in the real fixtures. Only the prefix separates it.
No prefix exists for AWS secret keys — entropy plus the key NAME is all there is. Sits in the same object as POS-aws-access-key-id, so a detector can also use co-location.
Pairs with NEG-bearer-as-english: the prefix must require a credential-shaped value AFTER 'Bearer ', not the bare word.

expectedFindings.shape: JWT — three base64url segments separated by '.'; segment 1 decodes to {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}
expectedFindings.sentinelNote: The payload base64url-decodes to JSON containing "sub":"SYNTHETIC-FIXTURE" — so the sentinel survives decoding, and a responder who decodes the token sees it is a fixture.

expectedFindings.shape: postgres-scheme URL carrying a userinfo component — user:password before the @, then host:port/db
expectedFindings.why: 🔴 NOT IN `env`. The credential is a positional command argument. Its `env` object is empty — exactly what every real config on the reference machine looks like. A detector that scans only `env` objects reports this server CLEAN.

expectedFindings.shape: https-scheme URL carrying a userinfo component — user:password before the @
expectedFindings.why: 🔴 ALSO NOT IN `env`. An http-type server def has no `env` key at all (observed shape is {type, url}), so the credential lives in the only field there is.
Project-scope MCP env. All 12 project-scope MCP configs on the reference machine had EMPTY env objects — this is the first positive at that scope.

🔴 THE PURE ENTROPY CASE. No known prefix, no recognisable shape, an unremarkable key name. If the entropy heuristic is dropped, this is the finding that disappears — and unbranded service tokens are the common real-world case.

expectedFindings.shape: PEM block delimited by BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY markers
expectedFindings.why: A MULTI-LINE value stored as a JSON string with \n escapes. A line-oriented scanner that never unescapes JSON strings sees one long line and may miss the BEGIN marker; a JSON-aware scanner sees it immediately.

expectedFindings.shape: postgres-scheme URL carrying a userinfo component — user:password before the @, then host:port/db
expectedFindings.why: DELIBERATELY THE SAME STRING as POS-postgres-url-in-args, in a different file and a different scope. One credential, two locations: the report must list BOTH sites. A detector that deduplicates by value hides a leak the user still has to fix in two places.

docs/02-architecture.md §4.2 declares `sync_token` as `sensitive: true`, routing it to the macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json. A literal here means that routing was bypassed — a finding on its own, independent of the value's shape, and detectable by cross-referencing the plugin manifest's `userConfig`.
expectedFindings.shapeCaveat: pluginConfigs nesting is UNVERIFIED — see ../precedence/README.md. The FINDING is real regardless of nesting; only the location expression depends on the inferred shape.

expectedNonFindings.why: Sits in the same env object as two real positives. Proves the detector reports per-VALUE, not per-object.
Empty env — the shape of every real env object in the corpus.
Every args array except synthetic-postgres's holds only flags and npm package names.
A URL with no userinfo component. Pairs with POS-basic-auth-in-url: the discriminator is `user:pass@`, not `https://`.
Indirection. Its key name mentions TOKEN and its referent IS a positive elsewhere — a key-name heuristic flags it, a value heuristic does not.
The sanctioned pattern (architecture §4.2). Flagging it makes the approved path unusable.
A real CLAUDE_* feature toggle — one of the three key names actually observed in settings.json env.
Indirection with a token-ish key name.
Empty value with a token-ish key name — the exact combination a key-name-only heuristic flags.
🔴 THE PAIRED CONTROL for POS-plugin-config-sensitive-literal: identical key, identical plugin-config position, correctly configured. If both flag, the detector is reading key names, not values.
A git URL with no userinfo.
The whole file. 15 values that must all clear. See its `entropyFinding` block.

byHeuristic.__note: Sums exceed 17 because most findings satisfy more than one heuristic. The load-bearing counts are the SINGLE-heuristic findings: prefix-only = 2 (POS-github-token-legacy, POS-aws-access-key-id), entropy-only = 2 (POS-aws-secret-access-key, POS-generic-service-token), shape-only = 4 (POS-postgres-url-in-args, POS-basic-auth-in-url, POS-pem-private-key, POS-db-url-in-settings-env). Drop any one heuristic and a specific, named finding disappears.

counts.__notInEnvNote: 3 of 17 findings are NOT inside any `env` object (two in args/url, and the pluginConfigs one). Scanning only `env` scores 14/17 and reports two servers clean that are not.
